dataset_info.summary: Audio from theatrical films, hand-labelled for when a human is speaking, with music, crowd noise and sound effects running underneath. One row is a fixed-length window cut from that timeline and labelled speech or not-speech. The soundtrack swells and crowd murmurs under the dialogue are the kind of audio that provokes a detector into reporting speech where there is none.
dataset_info.notes: AVA-Speech (frame-labelled Hollywood-movie audio) via the nccratliri/vad-human-ava-speech mirror — paired <clip>.wav / <clip>.json files under 'test/' and 'train/', each json giving parallel onset/offset arrays for human-speech segments across a multi-minute clip. Registered against the 'test' split (2 clips) as the smaller of the two. The clips are English-language theatrical films with mixed background music/noise/crowd audio; the mirror carries no per-clip language metadata and lang is genuinely mixed/incidental to the task (this is a VAD false-accept stress test on real cinematic audio, not a speech corpus), so lang is set to the dominant production language en-US rather than 'multi' per the fallback in the integration brief. This mirror already reduces AVA-Speech's four-way condition taxonomy (clean speech / speech+music / speech+noise / no-speech) to a binary human_SPEECH timeline -- the three speech conditions are exactly what a human_SPEECH onset covers, no-speech is everything else -- so reference_fields.format='ava-onset-offset' just flags runner.audio_io._stream_ava_speech to slice fixed-length speech/non_speech windows out of the onset/offset timeline (see that function's docstring); no further label mapping needed. A clip with zero AVA_SPEECH onsets is unlisted here since the 'human_' filename prefix implies the corpus only ships clips with human-attributed speech, but the adapter still yields non_speech windows from the silent gaps around and between segments.
